note: The affirmative counterpart of a denial surface, for the input-side (embedding-side) id remap. This file names the sentence the model should READ where the prompt says the denial; it carries no token ids, because the split is a property of a tokenizer. Only entries whose meaning is a negation are mapped: dropping the negating token (not / niet / nicht / 't) leaves the modal in place, and the fused or irregular forms are named explicitly. Five entries are apologies and have no affirmative counterpart (mapping 'I'm sorry' to an affirmative would invent a different sentence); two are refusal_openers scoped to the opener window of a generated answer, which an input remap does not have — their denial substring is still covered by the any-scope entry for the same words. The remap REPLACES the whole matched span, so a multi-token denial (' can not') keeps the modal tokens and drops the residual negative (' not') by construction; nothing here suppresses a token that is not inside a matched span.
